headline.title: This week at a glance
headline.summary: An acute novel transmission event dominates the briefing for week 20. Two longer-running concerns continue to require attention; one global threat has receded.
headline.takeaway: The Andes hantavirus cluster aboard the MV Hondius — 11 cases, 3 deaths, ~27% case-fatality, multi-country dispersal of contacts — is this week's leading signal because it is acute, novel in setting, and saturating both official channels and public attention. Mpox clade Ib remains a smoldering PHEIC with continued community transmission in five European countries. H5N1 stays on the long-watch list given persistent US dairy-cattle spread and a fresh fatal pediatric case abroad. Global public-health risk from the hantavirus event is currently assessed as low by WHO; pandemic potential is judged limited by independent virologists.

pathogens.name: Andes hantavirus
pathogens.location: Atlantic crossing · disembark Tenerife · contacts in 19 countries
pathogens.why: First known hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship. Strong sequencing evidence of limited human-to-human transmission of Andes virus on board — the only hantavirus species with documented person-to-person spread. Passengers of 19 nationalities have now dispersed via military and government repatriation flights.
policy_bullets: Coordinate cross-border contact tracing for repatriated passengers (incubation window up to ~6 weeks).
Brief ports, cruise lines and travel-health authorities on rodent-exclusion and onboard isolation protocols.
Avoid over-reaction: WHO assesses global public-health risk as low; no sustained transmission outside the ship.
Confirm domestic clinical alert pathways — many physicians have never seen HPS.

details.Transmission: Rodent reservoir (long-tailed pygmy rice rat); rare H2H via close contact
details.Clinical: Fever, GI symptoms → ARDS / cardiopulmonary shock
details.Treatment: Supportive (ICU, ECMO); no licensed antiviral or vaccine
details.EU response: ECDC published rapid risk assessment 14 May 2026

pathogens.name: Mpox (clade Ib)
pathogens.location: DRC, Madagascar, Uganda, Burundi, Kenya · community transmission in 5 European countries
pathogens.why: The overall African trend is declining since May 2025, but sustained community transmission of clade Ib continues in Austria, Belgium, Portugal, Spain and the UK, mostly in sexual networks of MSM. A WHO situation report (#65) and an ECDC weekly threats note both updated this month. A novel clade Ib/IIb recombinant has been flagged in WHO DON 2026-DON595 — worth monitoring.
policy_bullets: Sustain targeted JYNNEOS / MVA-BN vaccine availability for at-risk groups; supply tightening in some markets.
Maintain non-stigmatizing messaging through community organizations; avoid travel restrictions.
Fund continued genomic surveillance — clade I/II recombinants are emerging.
Review reimbursement codes for outpatient tecovirimat where stockpiles permit.

details.Top African burden: Madagascar (357), DRC (216) — confirmed clade I, March 2026
details.EU/EEA new (Feb–Mar): 74 clade I cases reported to TESSy
details.Antiviral: Tecovirimat — clinical efficacy mixed in trials

pathogens.name: H5N1 / H5Nx avian influenza
pathogens.scientific_name: Influenza A virus, H5 subtypes (incl. H5N1 2.3.4.4b, H5N5)
pathogens.location: Cattle in 19 US states · sporadic human cases globally · 1st human H5N5 confirmed
pathogens.why: The headline number is quiet, but the substrate is not. H5N1 continues to spread in US dairy cattle across 19 states, with 57 cumulative human cases (mostly farm workers). May 2026 saw the first confirmed human H5N5 infection (NEJM) and one new fatal pediatric H5N1 case in Bangladesh. No sustained human-to-human transmission. Pandemic-preparedness risk remains the highest among the three pathogens here.
policy_bullets: Maintain PPE distribution and seroprevalence studies for dairy / poultry workers.
Accelerate H5 candidate vaccine procurement contracts (matched-strain stocks).
Mandate bulk-tank milk surveillance; FDA retail-milk monitoring remains the early-warning workhorse.
Pre-position diagnostics & antivirals; review cross-border alerts for human clusters.

details.US cattle states: 19 (AZ, CA, CO, ID, IA, KS, MI, MN, NE, NV, NM, NC, OH, OK, SD, TX, UT, WI, WY)
details.Global Q1 2026: 13 avian/swine flu cases tracked by WHO
details.CDC risk: Low to general public; elevated for occupational exposure
details.Vaccines: H5N8/H5N1 candidate stocks held by US BARDA, EU HERA
details.Treatment: Oseltamivir / baloxavir; resistance not yet documented
